summary.text: Scott Peters is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for San Diego County's 50th District, first elected to Congress in 2012.

Before Congress he was an environmental lawyer, a San Diego City Council member and council president, and chair of the San Diego Unified Port District. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce and Budget Committees.

paragraphs.text: Peters was born in Springfield, Ohio, in 1958. He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and economics from Duke University in 1980 and a J.D. from New York University School of Law in 1984.
According to his official biography, he worked as an economist for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency before law school and then practiced as an environmental lawyer for 15 years.
Peters served on the San Diego City Council from 2000 to 2008, including as council president from 2006 to 2008; his official biography describes him as the city's first City Council President.

The biography says he helped lead the redevelopment of downtown San Diego and pursued a Council/Mayor form of government with an independent budget review function, and that he later chaired the San Diego Unified Port District.
In the November 2012 general election Peters defeated Republican incumbent Brian Bilbray in what was then California's 52nd District, 51.2% to 48.8%, and he was re-elected in 2018 and 2020.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Budget Committee; he co-chairs the Bipartisan Fiscal Forum and the House Special Operations Forces Caucus and chairs the New Democrat Coalition's Climate Change and Clean Energy Task Force.
According to his official biography, he and his wife live in La Jolla, where they raised a son and a daughter.
